What the numbers say

In this revision 98 option-selling candidates across 25 underlyings passed the report's filters, all of them short puts. Expiries run from 1 to 64 days out with a median of 8 days; 33 of the 98 expire within seven days and 6 are more than 21 days out.

The highest composite score is 74.7 for the SOXL 60 put expiring 2026-11-13 (1 day): premium $1.02, strike 7.4% below the share price, model probability of expiring out of the money 73.0%. Its displayed annualized yield of 620.5% multiplies a 1-day premium out to a full year, which is why the score discounts yields from contracts shorter than 30 days.

Implied volatility among the listed contracts is highest for SOXL (183.8%), SNDK (123.0%), IREN (116.3%) and lowest for COST (21.7%). High implied volatility is what makes a premium large; it is the market's price for a wide expected range, so the richest premiums sit on the names the market expects to move most.

Of the 37 underlyings with a quote, 12 were up and 25 down when the report was generated; the median move was −1.30%. Falling share prices raise the premium on offer for new short puts and, at the same time, the chance that existing ones are assigned.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-11), listed candidates went from 97 to 98 and the median time to expiry went from 9 to 8 days.

Backtest reference

The report carries a fixed reference backtest covering 2026-03-26 to 2026-04-22: 2,149 simulated option-selling trades with a 83.3% win rate and a profit factor of 0.70. A profit factor below 1 means total losses exceeded total gains even though most trades won. That is the characteristic risk of selling premium: many small wins and a few large losses. The window is short and does not include the session on this page; it is a description of that period, not an estimate of future results.
